$comment: BRAIN JSON REPLY (28 Oct 2026, brain-json lane) — the shape the hunt brain (AI or parent) sends when it is the brain. One reply = one step: WHAT it is doing now (task), the GOAL of the step, the PROGRESS so far, optionally a RECALL of one past action by hash/id, and exactly ONE ACTION to execute next. The schema carries NO full memory: progress is TITLES only, never full output; past detail is fetched on demand by hash (recall) or by id. The brain is never sent full memory — it sees the Action Index (one short line per action, #N + hash) and fetches a full record only when it asks for it. Validated server-side by backend/src/brainReply.js (hand-rolled, no new dependency — this file is the documented contract; the validator enforces the same rules). Field names in validation errors match the JSON paths below (e.g. 'action.command'). Action types map onto the existing brain-action dispatch in backend/src/brainMode.js (executeBrainAction): 'click' -> browser_click and 'type' -> browser_type; the rest keep their names. All guards apply to JSON replies exactly as to form-composer actions: scope, claim completeness gate, pipeline verifier, 404 error-page protection, owner-only auth.

examples.progress: Logged in as admin, security set to low; login page confirmed
examples.task: Probe reflected XSS in the DVWA search box

examples.task: Dump DVWA users via UNION injection

action.evidence: Hello <script>alert(1)</script> — marker PBRN7719 reflected in the page body, HTTP 200

action.description: Exactly ONE action, in the existing brain-action shape. 'type' selects the per-type fields below.

class.description: claim_finding: the vuln class, e.g. 'xss' — required — the validator refuses classless claims up front (the gate bounces them).

command.description: shell: the command to run. claim_finding: the exact command that reproduces the vulnerability (the verifier re-runs it).

confidence.description: claim_finding: how sure the brain is. Required by the claim completeness gate (with 'confidence_rationale' whenever it is not 'high').

confidence_rationale.description: claim_finding: why, when confidence is not 'high'.

counterevidence.description: claim_finding: what was checked that could have disproved this — the control/baseline result beside the trigger.

evidence.description: claim_finding: the exact output that proves it — a real excerpt of the response/output, not a summary or an assertion.

hash.description: recall action: content-hash of the action to recall.

poc.description: claim_finding (optional): name of a proof-script artefact saved in this hunt, instead of 'command'.

selector.description: click: the text/selector of what to click. type: the field to type into — its visible label, name, or CSS selector (REQUIRED). The driver focuses that field, clears it, types, and verifies the value landed before reporting success.

submit.description: type: press Enter after typing (default false).

text.description: click: the clickable text (accepted in place of 'selector'). type: the text to type.

title.description: claim_finding: one line naming the vulnerability.

type.description: 'shell' runs a command in the hunt container; 'browser_open' opens a URL in the hunt browser; 'click' clicks text on the page; 'type' types text into a named field (selector, required; optionally submitting); 'recall' returns a past action's full record; 'claim_finding' files a vulnerability claim through the completeness gate + pipeline verifier. OS CONTROL (28 Oct 2026): 'browser_snapshot'/'screenshot' read the browser; 'desktop_snapshot'/'desktop_click'/'desktop_key'/'desktop_click_at'/'desktop_click_control'/'list_controls'/'desktop_screenshot' drive the whole XFCE desktop; 'see_screen' is the vision loop (text map of the screen); 'desktop_terminal' runs a command in the visible terminal; 'launch_tool'/'download_tool' manage named tools; 'proxy_start'/'intercept_list'/'intercept_read'/'intercept_replay' are the intercept proxy (Burp-style).

url.description: browser_open: the URL to open (must be in scope — out-of-scope URLs are refused, nothing is opened).

window.description: desktop_click: the window title to focus. desktop_click_control/list_controls: the window to act in (optional for list_controls).

keys.description: desktop_key: one keystroke — modifiers ctrl/alt/shift/super/meta plus one key (Return, Tab, Escape, space, BackSpace, Delete, arrows, Home, End, Page_Up, Page_Down, F1-F12, or a single letter/digit), e.g. "ctrl+l".

x.description: desktop_click_at: the x coordinate from the see_screen map.

y.description: desktop_click_at: the y coordinate from the see_screen map.

goal.description: The overall goal of this hunt step — what 'done' looks like for this task.

progress.description: What has been done so far — compact, TITLES only (e.g. 'login done, UNION dump returned 5 users'), never full output. Full output stays in the action record and is fetched by hash.

recall.description: Optional: fetch ONE past action BEFORE acting. Exactly one of hash/id. The server returns its full stored record as 'recalled' alongside the action result.

hash.description: Content-hash of the action (from the Action Index).

id.description: Action number in this hunt's index: 7, "7" or "#7".

reason.description: Why you need this data (e.g. "I need the exact UNION payload that dumped the users, to reuse it on the next endpoint"). Recorded with the request in the process file. Optional in validation, always give it.

task.description: What the brain is doing NOW, one line. Shown live in the process view while the step runs, and recorded as the completed step when the action finishes.

title: BrainReply — one brain turn, as JSON
